bug_description.original_source: ARVO-Meta.report.comments[0].content / staged vulnerable source / saved sanitizer_trace.txt / patch.diff / reproduction_report.json
bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced an AddressSanitizer stack-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 11 in `io_memory_read` while the libFuzzer `ia_fuzz` harness executed `oba 0` on the staged 69,293-byte Mach-O witness. Along the crashing path, radare2's Objective-C class parser reaches `get_class_ro_t()`, sees a method pointer with low bit 1, and dispatches to `get_method_list_of_lists()` and `iterate_list_of_lists()`. `iterate_list_of_lists()` reads the 8-byte list-of-lists header, decodes an attacker-controlled `entsize` and positive `count`, and only checks that the mapped source region still contains `count * entsize` bytes. The local destination object for each element is `ListOfListsEntry entry`, an 8-byte stack struct (`image_index:16`, `list_offset:48`). Because the vulnerable code never checks `entsize <= sizeof (entry)`, it calls `r_buf_read_at (bf->buf, r, (ut8 *)&entry, entsize)`. The read flows through the memory-backed I/O path unchanged, so `io_memory_read()` receives `buf = &entry` and `count = entsize`; its initial `memset (buf, 0xff, count)` therefore writes 11 bytes into the 8-byte stack object, matching the saved ASan report. The fix adds explicit `entsize` validation against `sizeof (entry)` and caps the copy length with `R_MIN (entsize, sizeof (entry))`.

source.description: First project-side read of the specific list-of-lists header whose fields later become the overflowing per-entry length and loop count.
source.value_from: The staged witness is the specific 69,293-byte Mach-O file at `poc` (sha256 `b3a78bee0e48a12552dbc999149d4b97815752388f40fd75f9f76b1765dbd378`). The 8-byte header copied here is the one later decoded into `entsize = 11` and a positive `count` on the crashing iteration.

sink.description: ASan sink. The memory-backed read path receives `buf = (ut8 *)&entry` and `count = 11`, so this prefill `memset` writes 11 bytes into the 8-byte stack object `entry` before any truncation or source copy occurs.
sink.note: The saved ASan trace reports `WRITE of size 11` at `io_memory_read` line 82 and identifies `entry80` at `mach0_classes.c:674` as the overrun stack variable in `iterate_list_of_lists()`.

root_cause.description: The caller uses attacker-controlled `entsize` directly as the destination read length for fixed 8-byte `ListOfListsEntry entry` without checking `entsize <= sizeof (entry)`.
root_cause.note: The patch inserts `size_t mines = R_MIN (entsize, sizeof (entry))`, rejects `entsize < sizeof (entry)`, warns on mismatches, and reads only `mines` bytes here.

tainted_value_origin.description: This decode materializes the concrete tainted length that drives the overflow. On the crashing iteration it yields `entsize = 11`, which later becomes both the `r_buf_read_at` length and the `io_memory_read` `count`.

parser_admitted.code: get_method_list_of_lists (bf, klass->name, klass, (cro.flags & RO_META) ? true : false, oi, cro.baseMethods & ~1);
parser_admitted.description: The Mach-O Objective-C class parser has already decoded `cro.baseMethods`, seen its low bit set, and dispatched into the method-list-of-lists helper. The saved ASan stack `get_class_ro_t -> get_method_list_of_lists -> iterate_list_of_lists` proves the staged witness reaches this path during `oba 0`.

coarse_trace.summary: The harness writes the staged 69,293-byte Mach-O witness into a memory-backed `malloc://<Size>` file and executes `oba 0`; the crash occurs during this `oba 0` command before the later `ia` command runs.
While parsing Objective-C class metadata, a class record with `cro.baseMethods & 1` dispatches to `get_method_list_of_lists()`, selecting the vulnerable list-of-lists helper.

The helper reads a list-of-lists header, decodes `entsize = 11` and a positive `count`, validates only the mapped source extent, and asks `r_buf_read_at()` to copy 11 bytes into 8-byte stack local `ListOfListsEntry entry`.
The memory-backed I/O backend receives `buf = &entry` and `count = 11`; its prefill `memset` overruns the stack object and produces the recorded ASan stack-buffer-overflow WRITE.

fine_trace.note: Source. After the initial `va2pa()` mapping and header-size checks resolve the current list address, this call copies the 8-byte list-of-lists header into `tmp`. Those 8 bytes are the only direct attacker-controlled source for the `entsize` and `count` values decoded next.

The first 4 header bytes are decoded as the per-entry read length. On the crashing iteration this yields `entsize = 11`: the later read forwards this value unchanged to `io_memory_read`, and ASan reports `WRITE of size 11` at that sink.

The next 4 header bytes are decoded as the list entry count. The saved artifacts do not recover the exact numeric count, but the subsequent guard and the observed first-iteration crash prove it is positive and within `ST32_MAX`.
The count rejection guard is not taken, so the loop over list entries remains reachable for the decoded header.

The aggregate file-size guard is also not taken. This proves the mapped source buffer still contains `count * entsize` bytes from the current list header onward, but it says nothing about the fixed 8-byte destination object used for each element.

The current iteration's destination is stack local `ListOfListsEntry entry`. The type definition at lines 59-62 packs `image_index:16` and `list_offset:48`, so `sizeof (entry) == 8`; this local object is the exact stack variable ASan later reports as `entry80`.

For the crashing iteration, the immediately preceding `va2pa()` call at line 669 has already resolved the current element mapping, and these per-entry source-bound checks accept `entsize` as readable: `r + entsize <= bf->size` and `left >= entsize`. These are only source-availability checks; they still do not compare `entsize` against `sizeof (entry)`.

Root cause. This call uses attacker-controlled `entsize` as the requested read length while `&entry` still points to step 6's 8-byte stack object. The vulnerable source has no `entsize <= sizeof (entry)` guard here; the fix adds `size_t mines = R_MIN (entsize, sizeof (entry))`, rejects undersized entries, and caps the read to `mines`.

Sink. The `r_buf_read_at -> r_buf_read -> buf_io_read -> r_io_fd_read -> r_io_desc_read -> r_io_plugin_read` chain forwards step 8's caller buffer and length unchanged into the memory plugin, so `buf == (ut8 *)&entry` and `count == entsize == 11` here. This first `memset` runs before any truncation at line 90 and writes 11 bytes into the 8-byte stack object, overflowing `entry`; ASan reports `WRITE of size 11` and identifies `entry80` at line 674 as the overrun variable.

poc.trigger: The saved `ia_fuzz` harness writes the staged 69,293-byte Mach-O witness into a memory-backed file and executes `oba 0`. During Objective-C class parsing, `get_class_ro_t()` dispatches to `get_method_list_of_lists()`, `iterate_list_of_lists()` decodes `entsize = 11` for the crashing list entry, and the resulting `r_buf_read_at(..., &entry, 11)` request reaches `io_memory_read()`, reproducing the saved ASan stack-buffer-overflow WRITE.

format.name: Mach-O witness with oversized Objective-C list-of-lists entry size
format.contract: The witness is the specific staged 69,293-byte Mach-O file (sha256 `b3a78bee0e48a12552dbc999149d4b97815752388f40fd75f9f76b1765dbd378`). On the crashing path, Objective-C class parsing reaches `iterate_list_of_lists()` for a method-list-of-lists pointer, and the 8-byte list header at that address decodes to `entsize = 11` and a positive `count`. The mapped source span still admits 11 bytes for the first element, so `r_buf_read_at(..., &entry, 11)` is issued against the 8-byte `ListOfListsEntry` stack object.
